versions.localizedDescription:
Title music: lake6, fading out as soon as a save loads or a server is joined

- The menus play lake6 (the lofi one with OPTIONS > LOFI MUSIC on), fading in.
- It fades out as soon as any loading screen goes up: a save loading, a
  world being made, a server being joined or created. Cancelled back to the
  menus, it fades in again; in a game the world's music takes over.

Title screen: trees bending in the wind, clouds, logo intro and shine, SOLO / CO-OP, version

- title_background.png: six frames; the two trees bend with the wind
  (0-3 pixels at the top down to none at the bottom row), leaves flutter
  and the lake glitters, every 0.2 s while the title shows.
- title_clouds.png: three pixel-art clouds that drift across the sky,
  behind the logo, on the background's pixel grid.
- The logo drops in with a bounce when the title first opens (the boot
  splash is now the landscape alone) and catches the light every 6 s.
- The choices read SOLO and CO-OP, with one trainer and two trainers left of
  the words; the cursor sits by the chosen row's trainers. The mode labels
  elsewhere follow (SOLO, CO-OP).
- The version, small in the bottom right corner: CI and tools/ios_xtool
  write build_version.txt next to build_id.txt.
- title_screen.gd on StartupSplash runs all of it; coop_menu.gd only asks
  for the intro.

Title screen: pixel-art logo and background, never stretched, animated

The title artwork was one 1536x1024 picture stretched to fill the screen,
logo included, and the boot splash stretched it too (stretch_mode 5 is
Ignore). Now:

- title_logo.png: the PokeWilds logo alone, 167x58 pixels, three colours
  plus transparency, taken off the old artwork's ~6.8 px grid.
- title_background.png: the landscape widened for phones (2.25:1), 230x102
  pixels in eight colours, as three frames side by side: leaves flutter and
  the lake glitters (colour cycling, so it loops without a jump). The title
  menu shows the next frame every 0.4 s while it is on screen.
- The background covers the screen keeping its proportions, the logo sits
  at the top keeping its own, both with nearest filtering.
- title_splash.png: both together for the boot splash, shown with Cover and
  no filtering, laid out like the title so nothing jumps when it appears.
- The old 1.6 MB artwork and the unused pokewilds.png/title_bg1.png scene
  references are gone; the title no longer loads a 6 MB texture.
Merge hud-cleanup: one look and one grid for the field HUD

Server: give up on an area before the player does

The flaky travel step in CI (run 39477428637): the server printed
"making new area 1,0..." and nothing more, the client gave up at
prepare_travel's 10 minutes ("travel to the next area failed"), and
the runner killed an orphaned Godot at cleanup: the area maker had hit
the snow-on-the-peak hang fixed in the previous commit.

It also showed why a hung area maker is a failure and not a fallback:
the server waited 15 minutes before handing the area to the player's
device, 5 more than the player waits. It now waits 8, so the device
makes the area while the player is still waiting (checked with a 5 s
timeout: the client made area 1,0 itself and travelled).
Merge move-learn-preview: tap a move to read it before replacing it

Sideloading source for Feather, AltStore and SideStore, updated with each release

.github/source/make_source.py turns the published releases into an AltStore
source (apps.json) with every IPA, newest first. The new "source" job runs it
after publish and stores apps.json on the "source" branch, whose raw address
the README gives.

HUD: phone battery and a clock in the top left, switchable in OPTIONS

- OPTIONS > DISPLAY: BATTERY (on/off, listed only where a battery can be
  read: the iPhone build) and CLOCK (off / real time / game time), saved in
  game.ini like the other options. On touch, a tap on the clock switches
  real time and game time.
- The HUD sits right of the minimap (or at the safe-area corner without it)
  and hides with it under menus, battles and top panels. Game time is the
  CLOCK structure's (world.clock_minutes()), drawn in gold. Texts change at
  most once a second (game time) or every 10 s / at the minute.
- iOS: a small Godot iOS plugin (project/ios/plugins/pokewilds_battery)
  keeps UIDevice's battery in POKEWILDS_BATTERY, read with
  OS.get_environment; no Godot headers. Its library is built before the
  export in the ios job (xcrun) and in tools/ios_xtool (Swift's clang),
  where Package.swift links it. Desktop and server read nothing and show
  no battery.
- server/status_hud_test.gd: the HUD, options, game.ini and the clock tap
  in a real game (headless, throwaway data folder).

CI: faster builds (Mac job alongside the smoke test, LTO and import caches)

- ios no longer waits for smoke; publish needs smoke instead, so only a
  pack that passed the smoke test is still released.
- The engine is LTO bitcode recompiled at every link: Apple's ld and xtool's
  lld keep their LTO cache between runs (keyed on the engine profile and the
  linker).
- Godot's import cache (.godot) is restored in smoke, ios, ios_xtool and
  server: only changed assets are imported again.
- ios_xtool: no disk cleanup (the runner has ~80 GB free).
- The server smoke test prints as it goes, to see where its 5 minutes go.
xtool: do not fail at the end where there is no wslpath [skip ci]
